### 13.7 Tooling consequences: face routes and the component library
- V1 Generic-holding contracts (the `u_types` and `y_types` declarations) are a structural customer of computed interface connections, which are therefore prominent in this section.
- V2 D-062 makes three tooling commitments for them, namely the passthrough helpers' predicate, the routes `show(::Structure)` prints for each face (the name a port wears on its component's boundary), and a standard library of components, the units of modeling. [D-062]
- V3 The section covers the predicate and the face routes first, then the standard component library and the component test rig.
- V4 The passthrough helpers take a predicate.
- V5 `select` is the third selector beside `except` and `only`, on `input_passthrough` and `output_passthrough` alike (§8.8, D-251). [§8.8, D-251]
- V6 It stays explicit at the declaration site, evaluated at build, and printable.
- V7 That is the blessed (explicitly sanctioned where a neighboring practice is forbidden) side of the auto-bubbling line, where the author writes down the rule and the build evaluates it into inspectable data.
- V8 Auto-bubbling means promoting an unconnected input automatically to a root input, one of the root component's own input faces (D-322). [D-322]
- V9 Every artifact renders itself through `show` (§9.2, D-257). [§9.2, D-257]
- V10 `show(::Structure)` owes face routes (D-257). [D-257] (bold)
- V11 For every root face, that means the resolved chain down to the producing terminal, printed as one line per chain (`crashed → aircraft/crashed → aircraft/monitor/out`).
- V12 Once faces are computed rather than hand-listed, "what does this face actually reach" is a question the artifact must answer, not the reader.
- V13 `show(::Structure)` derives each face's routing chain from the declared wires and prints the root's routes (D-257, D-315). [D-257, D-315]
- V14 Each line joins the hops with `→` and ends at the terminal.
- V15 An input face that fans out prints one line per consumer.
- V16 The wiring diagnostics name endpoints in the same slash form.

#### The standard component library
- V17 A standard component library makes good on the junction promise (§6.2). [§6.2]
- V18 That promise rests on explicit junctions being cheap.
- V19 A junction hand-written per arity per type is not cheap.
- V20 The junctions, summing junctions and Bool gates alike, are the library's seed (D-062). [D-062]
- V21 A block joins the library's inventory by judgement against three guidelines (D-313). [D-313] (bold)
- V22 The guidelines ask whether a block is domain-agnostic and generally useful, whether it has didactic value, and whether its implementation is difficult to get right.
- V23 None is a requirement.
- V24 They are weighed, not satisfied one by one, and a listed block is built whenever wanted.
- V25 The inventory, and the Simulink mapping that prunes it, is `companions/library_inventory.md`.
- V26 A one-line expression such as a gain earns no block, because a separate component costs a build entry, a cell, a gather and a scatter (§9.7). [§9.7]
- V27 Domain components, such as aerodynamics, engines or sensors, belong in separate packages built on the framework.
- V28 Simulink's library is a language, while this is a toolbox.
- V29 The starting inventory holds the `Junction`, with `SumJunction{V, N}`, `Or{N}` and `And{N}` as its named forms, `UnitDelay{V}`, `Constant{V}`, `Freeze{V}` and `StopRequest`.
- V30 The shipped list lives in `companions/library_inventory.md`.
- V31 `UnitDelay` is the spelling the second loop-breaking remedy (§5.5) needs. [§5.5]
- V32 `Constant{V}` is the source block (D-143). [D-143]
- V33 `Freeze{V}` is the declared stop-gradient (D-266). [D-266]
- V34 `StopRequest` is the library spelling of a stop request (a port that ends the run when it reads `STOP_REQUESTED`) (§13.5, D-316). [§13.5, D-316]
- V35 The request is its port's `StopFlag` type, which any component may publish, so the block holds no privilege.
- V36 The library is the submodule `Redstone.Blocks`, `Group` included, written against the extension-only surface (§8.1) as a user's component file is (D-313). [§8.1, D-313]
- V37 A workspace sub-package or a separate repository is an after-release question.
- V38 One member is admitted by persona.
- V39 `Group` is the on-the-fly assembly (pure composition, with no dynamics of its own), and its declaration-layer treatment lives in §8.5 (D-184). [§8.5, D-184]
- V40 `Group` serves the model assembler, for whom topology is data rather than a named type.
- V41 It needs no rule the declaration layer does not already have.
- V42 The doctrine is that library blocks are ordinary components, with no framework privileges and no special vocabulary (D-062). [D-062] (bold)
- V43 Ordinary status is what keeps schema authority total (declarations define structure; evaluation only checks conformance).
- V44 That same status makes the library a permanent ergonomics torture test, a maximally awkward case spelled against the declaration rules to validate them.
- V45 If a three-input OR gate is painful to write under the declaration rules, the rules are wrong.
- V46 Arity and port types come from type parameters (D-311). [D-311] (bold)
- V47 `Junction{In, Out, N, F}` builds `(in1 = In, …, inN = In)` programmatically and applies the fold its instance holds, so `Or{N}` is the junction at `|` and `And{N}` at `&`, each a constant alias.
- V48 A gate exists for its consumer, which wants one consolidated `Bool` input instead of several.
- V49 That is a derivation §8.2 blesses, and an early validation that the contract functions support parametric components. [§8.2]
- V50 [code block] struct Junction{In, Out, N, F} <: AbstractComponent
- V51 The parameters are the nominal port types and the arity, as in `SumJunction{Wrench{Float64}, 3}`, and the fold is instance data (D-311). [D-311]
- V52 `Wrench` is FlightPhysics' force-and-torque type, here parametrized by its scalar type as a walked type of §7.2. [§7.2]
- V53 `SumJunction{V, N}` is the `Junction` at `+`.
- V54 A custom fold, such as a weighted blend or a mass-properties composition, is written at the site as `Junction{In, Out, N}(f)`, which infers `F`.
- V55 The junction is a continuous leaf, so its contracts are written at nominal `Float64` and the leaf walk retypes them (§8.2, D-263). [§8.2, D-263]
- V56 An input entry at `Wrench{Float64}` is the tolerant form a promoting consumer writes.
- V57 Walking, frozen and root-input contributors are all admissible behind it.
- V58 A named site-specific junction documents a fixed contributor set better than generated slots, at the price of hard-coding it into a type (D-037). [D-037]
- V59 An example is `u_types(::VehicleWrenchSum) = (aero = …, ldg = …, pwp = …)`.
- V60 The generic positional form remains the tool for configuration-variable sites.
- V61 Both are plain components, and the framework is not involved.
- V62 Wrench, mass properties and internal angular momentum each get their own junction, never one bundled contribution struct (D-037, D-323). [D-037, D-323] (bold)
- V63 Contributors are ragged, each publishing only some of the three quantities.
- V64 A bundled struct would force zero-filled identity values through every port, the "silently sum nothing" hazard in a new coat.
- V65 A `sum_ports!`-style helper would instantiate a junction, wire it and export its total in one call.
- V66 Such a helper is guarded-addition sugar (a capability the design admits but does not build), added when real models show the pattern repeated (D-037). [D-037] (bold)
- V67 Tier-transparency falls out of settled semantics (D-062), a tier being the continuous or discrete side of the hybrid formalism. [D-062]
- V68 A stateless continuous `y_direct` recomputes every sweep (one pass through the execution order).
- V69 Fed discrete signals held by a zero-order hold, its output therefore changes only at ticks (the instants at which a discrete component's stages and update run).
- V70 No tier-neutral class is needed.
- V71 `UnitDelay{V}` is a discrete leaf at `K = 1`.
- V72 It is the tier's native `z⁻¹` (§10.6), the shape an anti-windup chain's previous-saturation port hand-writes (`companions/pid_anti_windup.md`). [§10.6]
- V73 It needs no framework support.
- V74 [code block] # UnitDelay{V} — a discrete leaf at K = 1; its initial value is instance data
- V75 The delay holds its initial value as instance data (D-312), so `UnitDelay(v0)` needs no `zero` method on `V`. [D-312] (bold)
- V76 The store is isbits by rule (D-231), which bounds `V`. [D-231]
- V77 `UnitDelay`'s tier semantics are the point, and they must be stated wherever the remedy is recommended (D-348). [D-348]
- V78 Inserting a `UnitDelay` into a continuous loop moves that signal onto the discrete tier and inserts a `Δt_base`-scale zero-order hold into the model's mathematics.
- V79 That is a modeling decision, because the delayed signal is genuinely sampled rather than a transparent wire.
- V80 The cycle diagnostic (§13.8) therefore says so rather than offering the remedy as free. [§13.8]
- V81 `Constant{V}` is the source block (D-143). [D-143]
- V82 It has no inputs, no state, and a stage-1 body returning the value the instance holds.
- V83 [code block] # Constant{V} — a stateless continuous leaf; its value is instance data
- V84 `Constant` is a stateless continuous leaf, so the tier-transparency argument above already covers discrete consumers.
- V85 No discrete variant is needed (D-143). [D-143]
- V86 The leaf is deliberately pinned at that value's own type (D-312), because the block's output is its stored value. [D-312] (bold)
- V87 A `Constant{Float64}` declares a `Pinned{Float64}` port and means it.
- V88 A constant is never seeded, so it carries zero partials under any `Dual` activation (the build's typed products at a given scalar type), and the pinned port says so where a walking one would promote the value and declare less.
- V89 The honest pin is spelled rather than inferred.
- V90 The same holds for every library block whose output depends on neither its continuous state nor a walking input, such as a step source or a relay, and each declares its `out` pinned (D-312). [D-312]
- V91 Two uses need `Constant`, though a listed block needs none to be built (D-313). [D-313]
- V92 The zero-contributor configurations (§6.2) are one. [§6.2]
- V93 There, a required aggregate input has no physical contributor, and the zero total must be spelled as a wire.
- V94 The rig stub below is the other.
- V95 The block's value is instance data, like junction arity, not an overridable default (D-143). [D-143]
- V96 A configuration wanting an externally settable source uses a root input (§11.3), which keeps the block from drifting into a back-door input default. [§11.3]
- V97 A handle that references bulk data never enters as a root input, only through a constant source (§14.9, D-364). [§14.9, D-364]
- V98 `Freeze{V}` is the declared stop-gradient (D-266). [D-266]
- V99 It feeds a walking producer into a pinned entry, which the walk clause (§6.1) otherwise refuses. [§6.1]
- V100 [code block] # Freeze{V} — a stateless continuous leaf; tolerant in, pinned out
- V101 At nominal the strip is the identity, so the block costs one gather and one scatter.
- V102 `V` is a `Real` or a `StaticArray` of them, constrained at the type (D-312), so a struct-valued freeze is refused at the spelling until a model needs one. [D-312] (bold)
- V103 Under a `Dual` activation it drops the partials, and its output satisfies the pinned entry.
- V104 What the wire then declares is a zero coupling in every Jacobian along that path (D-266), the modelling decision §14.10 asks an author to state on the page rather than bury mid-expression. [D-266, §14.10]
- V105 A sampler is the other non-walking source, and it changes the model, holding the value between ticks (§10.5). [§10.5]
- V106 The block is for a continuous value the consumer cannot differentiate through.
- V107 Where the coupling matters to the Jacobian, the local rule (§14.10) is the answer, not this block. [§14.10]

#### The component test rig
- V108 The component test rig is the library's companion idiom.
- V109 Exercising a leaf alone needs no rig of its own.
- V110 Any component may be the root of a build, and its input faces then become the model's root inputs (§8.2, D-208). [§8.2, D-208]
- V111 Ordinary conditions and devices (attached participants in the periphery) feed them, and every output is observable in the table of each snapshot, the immutable per-boundary publication.
- V112 The rig is a one-child assembly whose `input_wires` surface the child's entire input face set, as `input_passthrough(rig, "child")` verbatim (§8.8). [§8.8]
- V113 What it buys is a place to wire something beside the component under test.
- V114 The demonstrated need is the root-input rule (§8.2). [§8.2]
- V115 An abstract input entry (`terrain = AbstractTerrainField`, an illustrative name) cannot surface as a root input, because abstract-at-root is a build error, `AbstractAtRoot` (§8.2, Appendix C). [§8.2, Appendix C]
- V116 The rig therefore satisfies that entry inside the rig (D-120). [D-120]
- V117 In the sketch below, the component under test is `Strut`, an illustrative landing-gear strut whose terrain input is abstract.
- V118 A concrete stub child (a provider of `SampleTerrainField`, an illustrative concrete terrain) is wired to the face, and the concrete remainder is exposed via `input_passthrough(rig, "strut"; except = ("terrain",))` (D-120). [D-120] (bold)
- V119 [code block] struct StrutRig <: AbstractComponent    # the rig: component under test + stub
- V120 That stub child is typically just a `Constant` holding the test handle, which makes it the source block's first shipped instance (D-143). [D-143]
- V121 Bespoke stubs remain ordinary components wherever the double must compute something.
- V122 The rig adds zero new machinery, because wiring and `except` already exist (D-120). [D-120]
- V123 It is the substitutability contract doing its job.
- V124 An abstract entry (an `u_types` entry admitting any concrete producer face) declares that a substitute must be chosen.
- V125 The rig chooses its test double explicitly, as ordinary inspectable code.
- V126 That is precisely the isolation the rig exists to provide.
- V127 The rig is `design_world`'s little sibling (§14.9). [§14.9]
- V128 Where `design_world(ac)` mounts an aircraft in a minimal world for trim and linearization, the rig mounts one component behind a root contract for unit tests and open-loop probing.
- V129 The machinery is deliberately ordinary end to end, with no framework support.
- V130 That makes the rig, like the library blocks, a standing ergonomics test of the declaration rules.

### 13.8 Cycle diagnosis: feedthrough tracing
- V131 The build rejects an algebraic loop (§5.5, D-005), and tracing is diagnostic only, never relied on for correctness (D-012). [§5.5, D-005, D-012]
- V132 Tracing improves error messages and verification.
- V133 When the build finds a cycle, it triggers the feedthrough tracer (the set-propagation instrument that tracks which inputs a value depends on) to classify that cycle.
- V134 A genuine cycle gets "break it with a state, a stage-1 (`y_state`) port, or a `UnitDelay`", and an artificial one gets the remedy ladder (§5.4, D-140). [§5.4, D-140]
- V135 Where the diagnostic recommends a unit delay, it states the delay's tier caveat rather than offering it as a free remedy (§5.5, §13.7, D-348). [§5.5, §13.7, D-348]
- V136 A tier is the continuous or discrete side of the hybrid formalism.
- V137 The parts below cover, in order, how a cycle is detected and named, the tracer's two modes, what tracing touches, how classification runs and decides, and the caveats and hints the diagnostic carries.

#### Detection and naming
- V138 A cycle surfaces as a topological-sort stall in the nominal evaluation, the build's second step and the one evaluation that feeds structure (§9.1). [§9.1]
- V139 The stalled subgraph is decomposed into strongly connected components (SCCs).
- V140 Each nontrivial SCC names one cyclic cluster exactly (D-012). [D-012] (bold)
- V141 Each cluster becomes one diagnostic, an `AlgebraicCycle` error (Appendix C). [Appendix C]
- V142 The diagnostic presents the cluster's members and the wires among them as one readable loop of terminal pairs in the canonical slash form (§8.6), as in `aero/F → dyn/F, dyn/a → aero/a`. [§8.6]
- V143 Neither the raw stall residue nor a single back edge names the cluster correctly (D-012). [D-012]

#### The tracer's two modes
- V144 The feedthrough tracer has two modes, and they degrade gracefully (D-349). [D-349] (bold)
- V145 Both are set-tracers.
- V146 A traced value carries a set of input indices, its tracer tags.
- V147 The global (value-blind) set-tracer is a `Real` subtype that carries a set of input indices, unioned by every operation.
- V148 It has may-depend semantics, a sound over-approximation.
- V149 A saturated `clamp` still reports, and $u^2$ at $u = 0$ still reports.
- V150 It is exact, in one evaluation.
- V151 It requires the traced stage-2 code to be free of branches and lookups on input-tainted values.
- V152 The sampled set-tracer (the local, primal-carrying mode) at sampled states is the fallback whenever the global tracer hits an undecidable branch, such as piecewise friction, stall blending or any gridded lookup at an input-tainted coordinate.
- V153 It reports the dependence pattern of the taken paths, sampled across randomized states.
- V154 Its only misses are untaken branches (D-012, D-349). [D-012, D-349]

#### What tracing touches
- V155 Only inputs are seeded (D-349), so branching on state, modes, parameters or time never interferes. [D-349] (bold)
- V156 Stage-2 functions also receive state views, but neither those nor the stage-1 hand-down are ever seeded.
- V157 Stage-1 functions are never traced, since there is nothing to seed.
- V158 Derivatives, guards (the declared functions defining each event's predicate), handlers and projections are outside tracing's jurisdiction entirely.
- V159 A known tracer blind spot is documented.
- V160 Value-severing operations pass dependence through a bare `Int` index, as a nearest-neighbor lookup does.
- V161 Linear and cubic interpolation are immune, because dependence flows through the fractional weights.
- V162 Dual-cleanliness in CI effectively guarantees traceability (D-349). [D-349] (bold)
- V163 Dual-clean means passing the `T = Dual` sweep of §7.2. [§7.2]
- V164 The guarantee holds because both modes ride the same `T <: Real` genericity as `Dual`, ForwardDiff's dual number.

#### Classification
- V165 Classification needs no execution order, the order in which the stage functions run (D-012). [D-012]
- V166 It runs inside the nominal evaluation's failure path, where no execution order exists.
- V167 None is needed, because each SCC member is evaluated once, in isolation, at the probe point (the initial state, where the build probes every user function).
- V168 That evaluation reads state views from the `x_init`, `s_init` and `m_init` declarations, out-of-cycle cell values from the acyclic prefix's probe values, and in-cycle cell values synthesized through `probe_value` (§9.3) under tracer tags. [§9.3]
- V169 The tracer's product is a per-member dependence set rather than a value, so no ordering has to be valid for the labels to come out right.
- V170 Classification touches no activation machinery.
- V171 There is no activation (the build's typed products at a given scalar type), no layouts and no table.
- V172 The cycle classifier uses the per-member (local) variant of tracing, the order-free per-member trace at the probe point (D-012). [D-012]
- V173 The "tracer activation" (§9.4) names the other variant (D-012), the global set-tracer run as an ordinary activation. [§9.4, D-012]
- V174 The two must not be conflated.
- V175 The per-member variant is not the sampled mode.
- V176 A member's map may come from either mode.
- V177 The traced maps decide the verdict as one graph question over the cluster (D-245). [D-245] (bold)
- V178 The verdict is the one §5.4 defines. [§5.4]
- V179 Every wire holds.
- V180 A hop inside a member runs from the face (the name a port wears on its component's boundary) that one wire enters to the port the next wire leaves.
- V181 The hop holds iff that member's map routes the face to the port.
- V182 The loop is real iff a cycle survives in that graph.
- V183 It is artificial iff none does, because every cycle through the cluster crosses a dead hop, at a component whose stage-2 function does not in fact route that input to that output.
- V184 The diagnostic lists every dead hop under either verdict, so a real loop still shows the chords the trace found false (D-245). [D-245] (bold)
- V185 For a simple cycle this reduces to the expected reading, that the loop is real iff every hop survives.

#### Caveats and hints the diagnostic carries
- V186 The diagnostic carries the tracer's caveats rather than assuming them away.
- V187 The trace speaks for the branch taken at the probe point, the diagnostic-only doctrine (D-012, D-343). [D-012, D-343] (bold)
- V188 Discrete members trace structurally, because the discrete tier's plain, wholesale-pinning declarations admit no tracer scalar (D-012). [D-012] (bold)
- V189 The remedy hint is offered only for continuous members (D-140, D-343), because structural tracing is sound as a may-depend answer but never sharp. [D-140, D-343] (bold)
- V190 The hops through a continuous face or port declared with no walking leaf trace structurally too (D-245, D-343), because such a face or port admits no tracer scalar either. [D-245, D-343] (bold)
- V191 A walking leaf is one whose type follows the activation scalar.
- V192 The diagnostic records the source of each member's map (D-245). [D-245] (bold)
- V193 The source is the global tracer, sampled states or structure.
- V194 A reader can thus weigh a dead hop found on a few sampled paths against one found exactly.
- V195 The hint itself is to split this component, or to narrow the neighbor's contract (its declared interface) when the dead hop's input is consumed only in a fallback branch.
- V196 Those are the ladder's two remedies (§5.4, D-140, D-343). [§5.4, D-140, D-343]
- V197 The build diagnostic offers both exits explicitly (D-140, D-343). [D-140, D-343]
- V198 For a loop between `systems/aero` and `systems/dyn` it reads "artificial at port level: `systems/aero`'s `F` does not route `a`; split `systems/aero`, or narrow the neighbor's contract if `a` is consumed only in a fallback branch".
- V199 The dead hop is the member's input face that its stage-2 function does not route to the output port.
- V200 The diagnostic carries the dead hop (D-245) as a separate field of its payload (the structured data a diagnostic carries) rather than dotting the hop onto the path (§8.6, §13.2). [D-245, §8.6, §13.2]
- V201 If a member's evaluation itself throws, the diagnostic ships with its members and wires alone, unclassified.
- V202 Classification is a bonus on the cycle error, never its precondition (D-012). [D-012]
- V203 ---
